options: The container every Fabric item — lakehouse, warehouse, notebook, eventstream, report — lives inside
A synonym for a single lakehouse
A per-item compute configuration

questions.q: What compute-related decision is made when creating a Fabric workspace, compared to Databricks?
options: Only a capacity assignment — no VM size, runtime version, or autoscaling bounds to configure
The exact same VM-size and runtime configuration as Databricks
Fabric workspaces require no compute decision of any kind, ever
Capacity must be chosen separately for every single item
questions.explain: The capacity assignment is a workspace-level setting, not a per-item one.

questions.q: What can a Contributor role do that a Viewer cannot?
options: Create and edit items, though not share them with others
Manage workspace-level settings and other members' roles
Nothing — Contributor and Viewer have identical permissions
Only Contributors can view items; Viewers cannot see anything
questions.explain: Admin can do everything including settings; Member can also share; Viewer is read-only.

questions.q: How do Fabric workspace roles compare to Unity Catalog's GRANT/REVOKE from the previous course?
options: They're a simpler, coarser, workspace-scoped version — applying to everything in the workspace at once, rather than per-table
They are functionally identical, just with different names
Fabric workspace roles are more granular than Unity Catalog's per-object grants
There's no meaningful comparison between the two systems
questions.explain: Unity Catalog's access control was per-object; Fabric's workspace roles apply more broadly.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe workspace concepts as feeling "familiar"?
options: Because they map directly onto concepts Databricks & Delta Lake already established, just under different names
Because Fabric and Databricks use the exact same underlying software
Because this is actually a review of the previous course's material with no new content
Because workspaces don't exist as a concept in Fabric at all
questions.explain: Recognizing the shape of a known concept under a new name is most of what learning a second platform involves.
